requirements.evidence: .env.example:1,7 set APP_NAME=PegaFila / APP_LOCALE=pt_BR; phpunit.xml:21-23 pin the three env values; config/mail.php:128-133 'markdown' => ['theme' => 'pegafila']; pegafila.css .button-primary uses #0f7490 (asserted inlined on the action button in tests/Feature/AccountEmailsTest.php:34,50); lang/pt_BR.json adds "Reset your password" and "Verify your email address"; routes/web.php:16-31 define password.request/email (throttle:6,1)/reset/update under guest and verification.verify with auth+signed+throttle; PasswordResetLinkController::store always returns back()->with('status', __(Password::RESET_LINK_SENT)); NewPasswordController::store rotates remember_token, fires PasswordReset and redirects to '/'; ResetPasswordRequest rules: min(8)->letters()->mixedCase()->numbers(), confirmed; VerifyEmailController uses EmailVerificationRequest (403 on id/hash mismatch) and redirects to '/'. Reset view has a single email input.

conventions.evidence: Inline $request->validate for the one-field forgot form and a Form Request for the three-field reset (matches the validation convention); PHPDoc on public controller methods; CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] and docs/business-rules.md updated. Deviation: the two auth views each hand-roll the full <html>/<head> boilerplate with the same Vite/CDN switch (forgot-password.blade.php:1-15, reset-password.blade.php:1-15) and repeated field markup rather than reusing Blade components.

security.evidence: No account enumeration: same status flash for known/unknown addresses (PasswordResetLinkController.php:28-32, tested); throttle:6,1 on password.email; guest middleware on reset routes; Password::reset validates token against e-mail; remember_token rotated; verification route is auth+signed+throttled and EmailVerificationRequest checks id and hash; all view output uses {{ }} escaping including the query-string email; forceFill limited to password/remember_token.

tests.evidence: tests/Feature/PasswordResetTest.php covers form rendering, guest-only redirect, registered vs unknown address (same response, no notification), validation dataset, 429 throttling, single email field, successful reset (hash, remember_token rotation, token deleted, event), invalid token, cross-account token, every password rule, missing token, authenticated block. EmailVerificationTest.php covers success, wrong hash, wrong id, unsigned, expired, already verified. AccountEmailsTest.php checks config pins, theme, subjects, button texts, pt-BR body, translated sub-copy and inlined #0f7490. Small gap: the verification mail test does not assert that actionUrl points to the verification.verify route.

simplicity.evidence: Controllers are thin and use framework facilities (Password broker, EmailVerificationRequest, Password rule object). Minor extras: the CDN Bulma fallback `@else <link ... bulma@0.9.4 ...>` duplicated in both views, and duplicated page shells.

readability.evidence: Small focused methods with clear names (PasswordResetLinkController, NewPasswordController, VerifyEmailController); descriptive test names; config comment block in config/mail.php explains the theme; no dead code or debug output.

scope.evidence: Almost everything serves the task. Unrequested: app/Models/User.php now `implements MustVerifyEmail` (changes behaviour of the Registered listener and `verified` middleware, which belongs to the registration/verification-notice tasks), and the external CDN stylesheet fallback in the views.

issues.explanation: Making User implement MustVerifyEmail was not asked for and turns on automatic verification mails on Registered and the `verified` middleware gate, which belong to the registration/verification-notice tasks.
Both views duplicate the full HTML shell and labelled-field markup instead of reusing Blade components, against the project's 'extract reusable markup' convention.
The hard-coded jsDelivr Bulma 0.9.4 fallback is speculative and loads a third-party stylesheet that may not match the project's Bulma version.
The verification mail test does not assert that the action URL is built from the verification.verify route, which requirement 5 states.

review.summary: The change implements the pt-BR account e-mails with a pegafila mail theme, the guest password-reset flow with non-enumerating responses and throttling, and the signed verification link, backed by thorough feature tests and docs/CHANGELOG updates. Remaining points are small: an unrequested MustVerifyEmail opt-in on User, duplicated view boilerplate with a CDN fallback, and a missing assertion on the verification URL, so it is approvable with nits.
